title: The M6.5+ share rose overall but fell within four preferred magnitude methods in global ComCat, 2000-2025
abstract: We compared the share of reported M5.5+ earthquakes that reached M6.5 in 2000-2012 and 2013-2025. The full global ComCat sample had 12,848 events. Its share rose from 8.94% to 9.56%. The change was 0.62 percentage points, with a conditional 95% three-year block interval of -0.56 to 1.88. Four common magnitude methods covered more than 98% of each period. Each method had a lower large-event share in the later period, although their combined share rose by 0.74 points. A symmetric split gave a within-method term of -4.81 points and a method-mix term of +5.55 points. Their block intervals were wide and included zero. The late centroid-moment group had only 121 events and three large events in two years. Thus the finite sample shows a reversal between pooled and within-method comparisons, but the adjusted time contrast is uncertain. Preferred methods depend on event size and processing rules. This split does not estimate a physical size change or a causal method effect. Code, aggregate counts, resampling draws, a count audit, provenance and a figure are included. External event records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Preferred method mix, large-event share by method, and the symmetric split. Bars and points describe the fixed four-method sample. Intervals use circular three-year blocks within each period. Weak method overlap makes the split uncertain.
